# PiTTy 1.2.1

This release includes the cache-aware compaction and Claude usage changes from 1.2.0. It also makes the usage-monitor test paths portable across Windows, Linux and macOS.

## Cache-aware compaction

- Use the active model and account to prepare a checkpoint from the original request context.
- Prepare compaction before estimated cache expiry by default, during a tool wait or an idle pause.
- Keep running tools alive. Apply the checkpoint at a safe boundary and retain later tool results and queued input.
- Choose **Cache-aware** or **Two-model extension** in Compaction settings. The extension choice is selectable only when it is loaded.
- Choose **Compact before expiry**, **Keep warm**, or **Off**. Existing explicit cache-maintenance preferences are preserved.
- Keep the one-round extension's configuration and `user_artifact` recovery tool when cache-aware mode is selected.
- Reject incomplete summaries and tool execution attempts. Do not impose a short side-question output limit.

## Claude usage

- Read usage from the account attached to each tab's native Claude process.
- Allow the native quota endpoint while keeping telemetry, error reporting, updates and native title generation disabled. Explicit user traffic restrictions remain effective.
- Display five-hour and weekly limits separately.
- Update readings when native usage changes. Mark retained readings stale after a failed refresh and show unknown values as `?`.
- Keep existing tabs on their original account when choosing an account for new tabs.
- Prevent delayed responses from another profile or an earlier request from replacing newer data.

## Extension updates

Required new extension modules trigger an update. Existing Git caches are checked first so tracked, untracked, ignored and unpublished work cannot be discarded by that update.

## Limits

The native SDK normally caches usage readings for up to 60 seconds and can return older cached data after a failed native fetch. Cache lifetime and remaining subscription allowance are separate measurements. Unknown cache lifetime does not start an expiry timer. A late timer after suspend does not force a cold automatic summary.

Native Claude retries hidden inside an active SDK request do not expose a safe checkpoint-application boundary. Automatic compaction covers idle pauses and tool waits. Keep-warm is reported unavailable for native Claude until it has a safe provider adapter.

Validation uses the real packaged runtime, terminal UI, and native SDK with isolated offline fixtures. It does not establish a live Anthropic cache-hit rate or compare real subscription accounts.
